findings.title: Task 7's inspection placement marks every rejected event as "progress", unbounding the dispatch retry loop
findings.description: Task 7 instructs adding the `RateLimitEvent` inspection "**before** the existing `ResultMessage.is_error` check" — i.e., after `progressed = True` (sdk_session.py:153), and never mentions `progressed`. Under sustained rejection (the exact scenario this slice exists for: "requests into a limiter that is rejecting them"), each attempt yields the rejected event, sets `progressed = True`, raises `RateLimitRejected`, and then `if progressed: retries = 0` (sdk_session.py:190) resets the counter — so `retries < MAX_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES` is always true and `dispatch` loops forever with 2-second sleeps, never exhausting the budget and never surfacing a rate-limit failure (criterion 5's "`progressed` reset unchanged" and criterion 6 are both defeated). The mandated test (Task 11: reject twice, succeed on the third, assert `call_count == 3`) passes despite this bug, so nothing catches it. The fix must either inspect before `progressed = True` or exclude rate-limit events from counting as progress — the agent path is already safe because `_skip_unparseable` raises before yielding. A persistent-rejection test asserting budget exhaustion is also needed.

findings.title: Task 6's informational-event instruction is self-contradictory (and mirrors a D4/D6 tension in the design)
findings.description: The bullet says to "continue the loop **without yielding** it to the caller … — **let it flow to translation as normal**". In `_handle_query_mode`/`_handle_client_mode`, translation only ever sees messages `_skip_unparseable` yields (agent.py:155-157, 203-206); an event that is not yielded can never reach translation. The LLD itself is inconsistent here: D4 says informational events "must not reach translation" (slice line 265) while D6 says the translation branch exists so an informational event becomes "observable rather than dropped" (slice line ~305). The tasks must pick one resolution — it determines both whether Task 4's branch is dead code in the agent paths and whether translated rate-limit messages reach downstream consumers (see next finding).

findings.title: Other `sdk_type` consumers beyond `sdk_session.dispatch` are uncovered by Task 8
findings.description: Task 8 correctly adds `"rate_limit_event"` to `dispatch`'s exclusion tuple, but three other consumers of translated messages carry their own `sdk_type` exclusion sets that lack it: `review_client.py:263` (`output_parts` becomes the parsed review prose), `pipeline/summary_oneshot.py:139` (becomes the summary text), and `metrology/audit.py:542-559` (`parts` / narration). Under the D6 reading of Task 6 (informational events flow to translation), a rate-limit notice concatenates into review prose and summary text — exactly the issue-#23 defect class Task 8 says is "not optional". Task 8's instruction is only to "verify no other `sdk_type` exclusion list exists" with no fix task and no success check naming these sites. Either these exclusion sets need the same addition (with a test), or Task 6's skip-and-drop reading must be made explicit so these consumers are provably unaffected.

findings.title: Task 6's "both gates" wording misses the third `RATE_LIMIT_MARKER` use; criterion 6 hinges on it and on an unspecified exception message
findings.description: `agent.py` has three `RATE_LIMIT_MARKER in str(exc)` sites: the query retry gate (167), the query exhaustion classification that raises `ProviderRateLimitError` (180), and the client retry gate (216). Task 6 says "replace both … gates (in `_handle_query_mode` and `_handle_client_mode`)" and its success line names only the "retry gates" — leaving 180 ambiguous at best. If 180 keeps the substring test, it only fires when `str(RateLimitRejected(...))` contains `rate_limit`; Task 2 says `RateLimitRejected` gets "no behavior beyond subclassing" and neither Task 6 nor 7 specifies its message text. Task 10 then asserts `ProviderRateLimitError` is raised on exhaustion (criterion 6) — an assertion that fails on a plausible message like `"rejected"`. Specify all three replacements (or explicitly retain 180 with a required message), and pin the message `RateLimitRejected` is raised with.

findings.title: Commit markers after Tasks 6 and 9 sit on a red suite — test rewrites are deferred to Tasks 10–11
findings.description: After Task 6 (commit at line 66), `test_a_rejected_rate_limit_event_reaches_the_backoff` fails: its `MessageParseError` with a `rate_limit_event` payload is no longer re-raised (the special case is removed) and is skipped, so no backoff occurs and `ProviderRateLimitError` never rises. After Task 9 (commit at line 89), the four `test_the_shim_*` tests fail against the deleted shim. Both commits therefore land on failing tests, contradicting the requirement that `**Commit**:` markers sit at working, tested points. Interleave the corresponding test rewrites (Task 10's subsets) with Tasks 6 and 9, or move the markers to the points where the suite is green.

findings.title: Success criterion 3's `RateLimitStats.throttles` increment is unmet — and unmeetable — in the pipeline `dispatch` path
findings.description: Criterion 3 requires that a rejected event "reaching any of the three dispatch paths" increments `RateLimitStats.throttles`, and Task 15's forced-throttle observation says to confirm it. But `SDKExecutionSession` has no `RateLimitStats` at all (it imports only `MAX_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES`, `RATE_LIMIT_MARKER`, `install_rate_limit_parser_shim`, `rate_limit_backoff_s`), and `dispatch`'s retry loop logs the WARNING and sleeps without recording anything. The LLD's D4 claim that all three loops already carry "… `RateLimitStats`" is inaccurate for this loop. Either add a stats counter to `SDKExecutionSession` (and assert it in Task 11's tests) or amend criterion 3/Task 15 to scope the stats observable to the agent paths; as written an implementer cannot satisfy the criterion here.

findings.title: Task 3's suggested test text collides with Task 10's verification grep
findings.description: Task 3 places `_is_throttle(ClaudeSDKError("rate_limit_event: slow down"))` in `tests/providers/sdk/test_agent.py` (its suggested location), but Task 10's success criterion is `grep -n "MessageParseError.*rate_limit\|ClaudeSDKError(\"rate_limit_event" tests/providers/sdk/test_agent.py` returning no matches — which the Task 3 test trips. Use a plain-429-style message that contains `rate_limit` but not the `rate_limit_event:` fabrication prefix (e.g. `ClaudeSDKError("429: rate limit exceeded")`), or move the classifier unit tests to a separate module. Relatedly, after the Tasks 10–11 rewrites no test drives the retry loop via the retained substring path (criterion 7 is covered only at the `_is_throttle` unit level) — one loop-level test using a genuine-429-style `ClaudeSDKError` would close that.

findings.title: Commit markers are checkbox lines after nearly every task
findings.description: `Commit:` markers appear as `- [ ] Commit: …` checklist items after 13 of 16 tasks (all but 12, 14, 15), rather than as plain `**Commit**:` lines at a few working, tested points. The checkbox rendering is defensible under the project convention that every item gets a `[ ]`, but the density is higher than "working points" implies and makes the markers toggleable items for `task-checker`. Consider consolidating markers to the true integration points (e.g. after Tasks 5, 9+10, 11, 13, 16).

findings.title: Criterion 2's `tests/`-half has no verification command
findings.description: Criterion 2 requires `install_rate_limit_parser_shim` to be gone from `src/` **and** `tests/`, but Task 9's success grep covers only `src`. The four shim tests referencing it are deleted in Task 10 (verified they are the only `tests/` references), so the work is covered — adding `grep -rn "install_rate_limit_parser_shim" tests` to Task 10's success line would make the criterion verifiable rather than assumed.
